Starting canvas…

Show the code two drawable screens, 3D cylinder curl shader, gutter spring, geometry sync and 2D fallback
  1. Two live drawable screens in one canvas. Both #view-list and #view-detail sit inside <canvas content="drawable" layoutsubtree>, with inert disabling whichever screen sits underneath.
  2. Analytic 3D cylinder page-peel shader. Renders #view-list at -24% to 0% parallax with a soft cast shadow, wraps #view-detail round the cylinder arc, and paints the shaded cream underside flap with faint bleed-through.
  3. Safe inset gutter threshold and spring settle. Restricts swipe starts to x <= 32 (unless Any-x swipe is enabled) and solves a damped spring on release to commit past 42% or cancel back to the detail screen.
  4. Hit-box calibration with geometryUnit(). Applies parallax translation to #view-list, flips inert and pointer-events cleanly, calls updateElementGeometry() and toggles dataset.hitTick.
  5. Five-argument 2D and plain-HTML fallbacks. Draws sliding parallax and a clipped peel lip using 5-argument and 9-argument drawElementImage() without WebGL 2, or extracts both views into plain HTML on context loss.

How it works

  • Both #view-list and #view-detail live inside one <canvas content="drawable" layoutsubtree> as direct drawable children. Because ElementGL holds one WebGL 2 context for the whole canvas, a single paint listener uploads changed views via gl.texElementSubImage2D() while active scrubs redraw the shader at display refresh rate without re-uploading unchanged DOM textures.
  • Browser back gestures on Android often trigger right on the physical screen edge. Here the phone viewport itself sits inside the page padding, and #view-detail shifts its buttons and inputs 38 px right of its left edge, leaving a 28 px inset rail inside x <= 32 where a dedicated touch-action: none strip captures horizontal drags cleanly without blocking central taps or vertical page scrolling.
  • The fragment shader divides the phone viewport at a rolling cylinder of radius R along the drag direction. Left of the cylinder roll, #view-list slides rightward from -24% to 0% parallax underneath a soft exponential cast shadow. Around the roll, the near face curves smoothly into a lit 3D cream paper underside with faint mirrored ink bleed-through over flat #view-detail.
  • Releasing a thumb drag evaluates both progress (> 0.42) and rightward flick velocity (> 420 px/s). A damped spring carries the curl smoothly to 100% or snaps it back to 0%, except when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (or the Reduced motion checkbox) is active, where release jumps straight to the final screen.
  • WebGL texture draws don't update Chromium's hit boxes automatically. Once a transition settles, syncViewGeometry() scales transforms by geometryUnit(), calls canvas.updateElementGeometry(), toggles dataset.hitTick to clear the hit-test cache, and flips inert plus pointer-events so controls on whichever screen sits on top answer clicks, typing and keyboard Tab order.
  • If WebGL 2 texElementSubImage2D() isn't available, the canvas swaps to a 2D context drawing sliding parallax and a vertical curl lip with 5-argument and 9-argument drawElementImage(). If HTML-in-canvas isn't enabled or the GPU context is lost, both views move into plain HTML until restored.

Findings

Not verified yet in headless Chromium 157 or Chrome 159 on Android. Tap "Run these 5 checks" above to measure this browser.

  • Not verified yet: real rendering, two-view texElementSubImage2D() uploads, cylindrical fold shading, updateElementGeometry() click routing, 2D fallback and touch drag behaviour at 412 px wide and scale 2.625.
  • Inset gutter vs OS edge swipe: placing the 28 px drag rail inside a 38 px left margin keeps central buttons and text fields safe from accidental drags while staying inward from the physical viewport edge.
  • State continuity across views: toggling "Mark as read" or "Pin thread" inside #view-detail updates #view-list's DOM immediately, so peeling back reveals the updated dot and badge gliding into place underneath.
